backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:124-176 — the payment auto-matcher's inner `for invoice in &open_invoices` loop (accounting.rs:129) creates a `PaymentMatch` for EVERY invoice whose confidence reaches the 0.5 threshold, with NO `break` after the first accepted match and NO in-memory update of `line.match_state`.

The outer per-line guard (`if line.match_state != "unmatched" && line.match_state != "suggested" { continue }`, accounting.rs:125-126) reads the DB-loaded `line` copy, which is never mutated inside the loop. The DB `update_bank_statement_line_match_state_rls(... "suggested")` call (accounting.rs:170) does not touch the local `line`, so subsequent iterations of the SAME line keep matching. Result: one bank statement line is suggested-matched to multiple invoices in a single pass.

Reachable precondition: two or more open invoices (status Issued/PartiallyPaid) that share the same non-empty `variable_symbol`. Variable Symbol alone contributes 0.8 (accounting.rs:135-138) which crosses the 0.5 acceptance threshold, so every open invoice carrying that VS produces a duplicate `PaymentMatch` (state Suggested) for the one incoming payment. Nothing in the schema enforces VS uniqueness across open invoices (partial payments, reissues, tenant data-entry errors make collisions plausible).

Consequence: duplicate/conflicting suggested matches for a single payment; a manager reconciling the statement sees the same incoming amount proposed against several invoices, and any downstream 'accept highest-confidence per invoice' step could book one payment against multiple invoices.
Fix: `break` after the first accepted match (or select the single best-confidence invoice for the line), and/or mark the line consumed in-memory so later iterations skip it.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:135-150 — a Variable-Symbol match alone contributes 0.8 and crosses the 0.5 acceptance threshold (accounting.rs:150) with NO amount corroboration required. The amount branch only ADDS confidence (+0.15 exact, +0.05 within-range, accounting.rs:143-146); a gross amount mismatch subtracts nothing.

So a bank line whose `amount` is wildly different from the invoice's `remaining_amount = total_amount - paid_amount` (accounting.rs:142) — e.g. a large credit against a small invoice, or an amount far exceeding the outstanding balance — is still suggested at 0.8 purely on the VS. The amount-only path can never reach 0.5 on its own (max 0.15), so acceptance is effectively 'VS matches, amount ignored'.

Combined with the multi-match bug in the same loop, this widens the blast radius: an incoming payment with a shared/reused VS but an implausible amount is proposed against invoices it cannot plausibly settle.

Fix: gate acceptance on amount plausibility (e.g. require `line.amount <= remaining_amount`, or withhold the suggestion when the amount exceeds the outstanding balance by a large margin) rather than accepting on VS alone; VS should raise confidence, not bypass the amount check entirely.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/delay.rs:53-61 — `DelayConfig::to_duration()` multiplies the config-supplied `duration: u64` by an unchecked constant per unit: `Duration::from_secs(self.duration * 60)` (Minutes, :57), `* 3600` (Hours, :58), `* 86400` (Days, :59). The multiplication has no `checked_mul`/`saturating_mul` and no upper-bound check on `self.duration`.

The 7-day cap that is supposed to bound the delay runs AFTER the overflow-prone multiply, not before: in `execute()` the order is `let duration = delay_config.to_duration();` (delay.rs:100) then `if duration.as_secs() > MAX_DELAY_SECONDS { return Err(...) }` (delay.rs:103-105). frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/errorHandler.ts:149-160 — parseApiError() runs isNetworkError(error) as its FIRST branch, before the structured-error branches (isAxiosError at :162, isErrorResponse at :205). isNetworkError (errorHandler.ts:394-416) does case-insensitive substring sniffing on ANY object's `.message`: message.includes('network') || message.includes('failed to fetch') || message.includes('network request failed') || message.includes('networkerror').

This misclassifies genuine structured backend errors as generic connectivity errors whenever the backend's human message happens to contain a network keyword. The transformed ApiError from lib/api.ts:152-169 is an Error instance whose `.message` is set directly from the backend body (`data?.message`), so an ApiError is exactly the object shape that trips isNetworkError. Concrete failure: backend returns 422 { error:'VALIDATION_ERROR', message:'Network name must be unique', requestId:'abc', details:[{field:'network_name', message:'...'}] }; the axios interceptor (api.ts:transformError) builds ApiError(message='Network name must be unique'); a UI calling parseApiError(apiError) hits isNetworkError → returns the canned NETWORK_ERROR ('check your connection') and DROPS statusCode, code, requestId, and validationErrors. The user sees a bogus 'connection problem' instead of the field-level validation, and error telemetry loses the requestId.

Root cause is ordering + heuristic scope: message-substring detection is only safe for the axios TOP-LEVEL error.message (e.g. 'Network Error' from axios itself), not for a field that also carries server-authored text. Fix: gate the network heuristic to the true no-response case (axios error with code==='ERR_NETWORK' or !error.response, and TypeError 'fetch' path) and move the generic message-keyword check AFTER isAxiosError/isErrorResponse structured parsing, or restrict it so a structured ErrorResponse (has `error` + `message` string fields) is never swallowed by the network branch. Add a regression test: parseApiError of a 422 ApiError whose message contains 'network' must return code='VALIDATION_ERROR' with validationErrors intact.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:81-97 — the subscribe effect early-returns when `!eventType || !handlerRef.current` and lists deps `[eventType, subscribe]`, intentionally excluding `handler` (handler is read via handlerRef to avoid re-subscribing on identity changes).

Edge case: if a consumer calls useWebSocket(eventType, handler) with a STABLE eventType but `handler` initially undefined (e.g. gated on a not-yet-ready callback: useWebSocket('message:new', ready ? onMsg : undefined)), the effect runs once at mount, sees handlerRef.current === undefined, returns without subscribing, and never re-runs when handler later becomes defined — because neither eventType nor subscribe changed. The subscription is silently never established, so realtime events for that eventType are dropped for the component's lifetime.

The optional `handler?` in the signature (useWebSocket.ts:74) advertises undefined as a supported input, making this a real API-contract gap rather than a misuse. Low severity because the common call site passes an always-defined inline handler; but the fix is cheap: include a boolean `hasHandler = handler != null` in the dep array (or subscribe unconditionally and no-op inside wrappedHandler when handlerRef.current is undefined) so a handler transitioning undefined→defined re-arms the subscription.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:753-763 — introspect_pm_token() caches active=false for the full 60s TTL on ANY non-success HTTP response from the PM introspection endpoint: `if !response.status().is_success() { ... state.token_cache.set(token, false, None, None).await; return Err(...) }`. A transient PM-API failure (503/502/500 during a deploy or overload) is thus conflated with a genuinely-inactive token.

Consequence: a legitimate, still-valid session token that hits the cache-miss path during a brief PM outage is negatively cached as inactive for up to 60s. Because introspect_pm_token feeds the SSO auth hot path, the user is denied/logged-out for up to a minute AFTER PM has already recovered — an availability regression driven by transient upstream errors, not by real token state.

The comment 'Cache inactive tokens too (to prevent repeated failed validations)' assumes non-2xx == inactive, but introspection RFC 7662 returns 200 with {active:false} for a genuinely inactive token; a 5xx is a server error, not an inactivity signal. Suggested fix: only negative-cache when the introspection call SUCCEEDS (200) and the body reports active=false; on 5xx/network errors, propagate the error WITHOUT writing a false entry (fail-open to a re-check on the next request, or short-TTL/no-cache).

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:682 (exchange_code_for_tokens), :706 (get_user_info), :743 (introspect_pm_token) — each SSO OAuth helper constructs a fresh `reqwest::Client::new()` per invocation. `Client::new()` has NO request timeout, so a hung/slow PM OAuth server on the token-exchange / userinfo / introspection calls will block the awaiting request indefinitely (only bounded by whatever axum/OS imposes), risking worker/connection exhaustion under a stalled upstream.

backend/crates/api-core/src/middleware/rls_context.rs:185-251 — `require_rls_context` is documented (lines 181-184) as 'a stricter version ... Use this for routes that MUST have tenant isolation', but it enforces NOTHING: it calls `db::tenant_context::set_request_context(pool.as_ref(), Some(tenant_id), Some(user_id), is_super_admin)` (line 232) then runs the handler via `next.run(request)` (line 245). `set_request_context<E: Executor>` (backend/crates/db/src/tenant_context.rs:18) issues its `set_config`/SET on a connection sqlx transiently checks out of the POOL and immediately returns; the handler later acquires a DIFFERENT pooled connection where the RLS GUCs are unset. Result: tenant-isolation is silently NOT applied to the handler's queries — a cross-tenant data-exposure footgun for any route that adopts this middleware believing the doc.

The module's own header (rls_context.rs:1-37) already diagnoses this exact defect ('Setting RLS on the pool doesn't affect individual connections'; 'PostgreSQL session settings are connection-scoped, not pool-scoped') and marks the module DEPRECATED — yet the file is not `#[deprecated]`, and BOTH broken functions plus `rls_context_middleware` are glob re-exported to consumers via `pub use rls_context::*;` (backend/crates/api-core/src/middleware/mod.rs:16). The contradiction (top says 'do NOT use'; `require_rls_context` docstring says 'use this for routes that MUST have tenant isolation') is the trap.

Not currently mounted in either server (grep of servers/ finds no call site), so severity is a LATENT bypass rather than a live one — hence confidence medium, not high. But it is live-ready API surface: a future route author who follows the `require_rls_context` docstring gets a compiling, plausible-looking guard that leaks across tenants with no error.

Fix: delete the deprecated module (the correct path is the `RlsConnection` extractor, which sets RLS on the same dedicated connection it hands the handler — see extractors/rls_connection.rs), or at minimum stop re-exporting it and add `#[deprecated]` + `compile_error!`-style guards; do NOT leave a function named `require_rls_context` that provides no isolation.

backend/crates/api-core/src/middleware/authorization.rs:170-201 — `require_permission` derives the caller role with `request.extensions().get::<TenantRole>().cloned().unwrap_or(TenantRole::Guest)` (lines 176-180). For an UNAUTHENTICATED request (no `TenantRole` in extensions) the role defaults to `Guest`, whose `level()` is 10 (backend/crates/common/src/tenant.rs:125).

`require_authenticated` (authorization.rs:236-241) delegates to `permissions::AUTHENTICATED = Permission::min_level(1, ...)` (line 139). `is_satisfied_by(Guest)` = `Guest.level() >= 1` = `10 >= 1` = TRUE. So the middleware literally named 'require authenticated user' GRANTS access to a request that carries NO authenticated identity — a fail-OPEN default. The higher-tier convenience guards (require_manager=80, require_owner=60, require_admin=90) happen to still deny Guest, so the hole is specific to the AUTHENTICATED gate, i.e. exactly the guard a route would pick to mean 'any logged-in user'.

Currently these from_fn-style guards are not mounted in servers/ (routes use their own `require_manager_in_org`/`require_platform_admin` helpers), so this is a latent footgun, not a live bypass — confidence medium. But it is public, documented, example-carrying middleware inviting adoption.

Fix: make the missing-role case fail closed — return 401 when no `TenantRole` (or authenticated principal) is present instead of substituting `Guest`, and/or give unauthenticated requests a role whose level is 0 that no `min_level(1)` permission satisfies. An authorization primitive must never treat 'no identity' as a valid low-privilege identity that clears an 'authenticated' check.

backend/crates/api-core/src/middleware/idempotency.rs:95-179 — `handle_idempotent_request` opens a DB transaction `pool.begin()` (line 95), takes a `pg_advisory_xact_lock` (line 108), and then HOLDS that transaction (and therefore one pooled connection) open across the entire downstream request: `next.run(request).await` at line 148, committing only afterward (line 177). The wrapped handler independently acquires its OWN pooled connection(s) (e.g. via the `RlsConnection` extractor) to do its work.

Concurrency hazard: with pool size N, N concurrent idempotent requests (distinct keys) each pin one connection in the still-open idempotency transaction and then each block waiting to check out a second connection for their handler — a classic pool-exhaustion self-deadlock; all N stall until acquire timeouts fire. Even below saturation this doubles the effective connection footprint of every idempotent (mutating POST/PUT) request and stretches the advisory-lock/transaction hold time to the full handler latency (including any slow outbound calls the handler makes).

The extensive comment at lines 80-94 justifies the xact-scoped lock purely for cancellation-safety (leak avoidance) and does NOT acknowledge the connection-held-across-handler cost, suggesting the pool-pressure interaction was not considered.

Fix: don't straddle the handler with an open transaction. Acquire the advisory lock + look up/insert a 'pending' ledger row in a SHORT transaction that commits before `next.run`, then persist the captured response in a SECOND short transaction after the handler returns (serialization is still provided by the ledger row / a shorter-lived lock). This releases the connection for the duration of handler execution and removes the deadlock/footprint-doubling.

Systemic across the commonMain repository layer: every repository that wraps a suspend Ktor call in try/catch uses a bare `catch (e: Exception)` and folds the throwable into `Result.failure(e)` WITHOUT first rethrowing kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException. In Kotlin coroutines, CancellationException is an Exception, so `catch (e: Exception)` swallows it — this breaks structured/cooperative cancellation. Affected files (57 catch sites total): favorites/FavoritesRepository.kt (11), auth/SsoService.kt (9), notifications/NotificationRepository.kt (9), inquiry/InquiryRepository.kt (8), listing/ListingRepository.kt (6), agency/AgencyRepository.kt (4), realtor/PortalListingsRepository.kt (2, lines 62 & 97), realtor/RealtorRepository.kt (2, lines 41 & 61).

The correct pattern already exists in this very codebase: shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/layout/LayoutRepository.kt:65-70 does `catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` immediately before the generic `catch (e: Exception)`. LayoutRepository is the ONLY of the 10 repos that handles this correctly (grep for CancellationException across commonMain returns only LayoutRepository.kt), which demonstrates the intended convention and that the other 9 repos are inconsistent regressions rather than a deliberate design choice.

Impact: when a composable's rememberCoroutineScope / viewModelScope is cancelled (user navigates away, screen disposed, or a newer request supersedes an in-flight one), the cancelled Ktor call throws CancellationException which is caught and returned as `Result.failure(e)`. Callers then treat a normal cancellation as a real error — e.g. Navigation.kt list loaders do `.onFailure { xxx = emptyList() }`, and screens like AccountScreen surface Log.e / error UI. This produces spurious error states/empty-list flashes on navigation and can interfere with cancellation propagation. Fix: add `catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` as the first catch clause in each suspend fun's try/catch (mirroring LayoutRepository), or centralize the request+Result wrapping in a shared helper that rethrows CancellationException. Recommend a follow-up implementer task to sweep the 9 repositories.

shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/layout/LayoutRepository.kt uses raw `println(...)` for diagnostic logging in commonMain (shared production KMP code) at three sites: line 48 ('falling back to default layout: HTTP ...'), line 57 ('...: unexpected screen echo ...'), and line 68 ('...: ${e.message}'). println in commonMain writes uncontrolled output to stdout on Android (logcat System.out) and to the device console on iOS with no tag, level, or ability to disable it in release builds.

It is the only repository in the commonMain layer that logs with println (the sibling repos either return Result.failure with a message or use platform loggers at the call site, e.g. AccountScreen uses Log.e). This is inconsistent and leaks internal fallback behavior to release logs. Fix: route through a shared expect/actual logger (or Kermit/Napier if already available), gate on a debug flag, or drop the println entirely since the fallback is already returned as DEFAULT_LISTING_DETAIL_LAYOUT. Low severity / cleanup, but easy and self-contained.

Compose screens repeatedly re-assert nullable UI-state fields with `!!` immediately after a `when`/`if` null-guard instead of smart-casting a locally captured val: androidApp/.../ui/listing/ListingDetailScreen.kt:121 (state.errorMessage!!), :125/:149/:160 (state.listing!!), :132 (state.listing!!.realtor?...); ui/account/AccountScreen.kt:174 (notificationPrefs!!); ui/inquiries/InquiriesScreen.kt:169 (errorMessage!!); ui/favorites/FavoritesScreen.kt:164 (errorMessage!!).

Because `state` is backed by a Compose State/StateFlow, the guard check and the `!!` deref are separate reads of a mutable property; a delegated-property `!!` after a `when (state.x != null)` is not protected by smart-cast and is a latent NPE-on-recomposition smell if the state can change between reads. The idiomatic fix is to capture into a local val inside the guarded branch (e.g. `val listing = state.listing ?: return@... ` or `state.listing?.let { ... }`) so the compiler smart-casts and the `!!` disappears. Repeated across 4 screens; low severity but a consistent maintainability/robustness cleanup for a follow-up task.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/AutomationRulesPage.tsx:56-72 — confirmDelete/handleToggle/handleRun each `await <mutation>.mutateAsync(...)` with NO try/catch, and the page renders error UI only for the list query (`error` at :178) — deleteRule.error / updateRule.error / runRule.error are never surfaced anywhere in the component.

There is no global mutation error handler to catch the rejection: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/main.tsx:28-35 configures QueryClient defaultOptions with `queries` only (staleTime, retry) — no `mutations` / MutationCache onError. So a rejected mutateAsync becomes an unhandled promise rejection with zero user feedback.

Concrete failure: confirmDelete (:56-61) — if deleteRule.mutateAsync rejects (network drop / 409 / 500), the throw skips `setDeleteConfirm(null)` (:59) so the delete-confirmation modal stays open indefinitely with the button re-enabled and no error message; the user cannot tell the delete failed. handleToggle (:63-68) — a failed enable/disable toggle reverts the switch visually on the next render with no indication the change was rejected, so the manager believes a rule is paused when it is still live (or vice-versa). handleRun (:70-72) and ExecutionMonitoringPage.handleRetry (ExecutionMonitoringPage.tsx:74-77) share the same no-catch/no-error-surface pattern.

Fix: wrap each handler in try/catch and render the mutation error (or add a MutationCache onError toast in main.tsx). Note CreateRulePage.tsx:62 and EditRulePage.tsx:113 DO render `createRule.error`/`updateRule.error`, so the list page is the inconsistent outlier.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/components/ConditionBuilder.tsx:211-218 — the number-typed value input does `onChange={(e) => updateCondition(index, { value: Number(e.target.value) })}`. `Number('')` is `0`, so clearing the field silently persists the condition value as 0 rather than empty/unset.

addCondition (ConditionBuilder.tsx:81) seeds every new condition with `value: ''`. When the selected field is numeric (e.g. 'payment.amount', 'payment.daysOverdue', 'document.size' — getFieldType==='number', lines 21-24), a user who adds a condition and never types a value, or types then deletes it, ends up saving `value: 0` with no validation gate anywhere in the builder.

Effect: a rule like 'Payment Amount greater_than 0' or 'Days Overdue greater_than_or_equals 0' silently matches essentially every record instead of the intended threshold — an automation that fires far more broadly than the author expects (e.g. dunning/notification actions sent to all payers). There is no min/required check and no distinction between 'blank' and 'zero' in the persisted TriggerCondition.

Fix: keep the raw string in state (or use `e.target.value === '' ? '' : Number(e.target.value)`) and block save (RuleBuilder canProceed) when a non-empty operator has an empty/NaN numeric value; mirror the string-input branch (:220-227) which correctly preserves ''.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/listings/LayoutSections.tsx — `SectionBoundary` (a minimal class error boundary wrapping every listing-detail layout section) implements `componentDidCatch(_error, _info)` with an empty body and the comment `// Intentionally swallowed — console.error suppressed by tests` (~:68). The error and errorInfo are discarded entirely: no telemetry, no logging, no error-reporting sink.

Behaviourally the boundary renders `<Placeholder />` on `getDerivedStateFromError` so siblings survive (good), but because the caught error is thrown away, a section component that crashes in production silently degrades to a blank placeholder with ZERO operational signal. A recurring render bug in one listing-detail section (JSON-LD, gallery, price block, etc.) would be invisible to monitoring — no way to know which section, on which listing, for how many users.

The stated reason ('console.error suppressed by tests') conflates test-noise suppression with production observability: tests can silence console.error via a spy without the component needing to drop the error. Fix: forward `_error`/`_info` to the app's error-reporting channel (or at minimum `console.error` outside test env) so section crashes are observable; keep the graceful `<Placeholder />` fallback. Low severity (reliability/observability gap, not a user-facing crash).
